```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  eval = FALSE
)
```

This article applies the full `cellprograms` workflow — donor-level EBMF
programs per cell type, covariate association, and cross-cohort MR-0 freeze /
MR-1 projection — to the 8-cohort PBMC immune-aging resource of Terekhova et
al. (Immunity 2026): **2,609 healthy donors** across ABF300 (166), OneK1K
(981), AIDA (625), CIMA (421), KCL (188), UCSF (99), SoundLife (96), and SPAC
(33), with 59 harmonized cell types. All numbers and figures are precomputed;
code chunks show exactly how each was produced and can be re-run against the
open portal data (see [Reproducing](#reproducing)).

The analysis answers three questions:

1. Do EBMF programs discovered in one cohort **transfer** to another (score
   concordance of projected vs refit programs)?
2. Which programs carry **age** structure, and does that structure replicate
   across cohorts?
3. At what level is conservation observable — scores, association profiles,
   or gene lists?

## Data and pseudobulking

Each cohort is downloaded from the authors' open portal and pseudobulked per
donor × cell type by summing raw counts over all cells (minimum 10 cells per
donor-cell type; the "Bad quality" annotation group is dropped):

```{r pseudobulk, eval = FALSE}
# per cohort, e.g. OneK1K (see analyses/immune_aging/README.md for access)
python scripts/pseudobulk_h5ad.py OneK1K_reannotated.h5ad pseudobulk/onek1k OneK1K --min-cells 10
```

The result is a donors × genes count matrix per cell type plus harmonized
metadata (donor_id, age, sex, ethnicity, CMV, BMI). CMV is informative only
in KCL and SoundLife; all cohorts carry broad age ranges (19–97 in OneK1K).

## Fitting programs (MR-0 discovery freeze)

Programs are fit per cell type with the default EBMF machinery
(point-Laplace loading prior), top-2000 variable genes, log1p-CP10K scale,
K up to 10, **without** covariate residualization — an amendment adopted
after a pilot showed that residualizing age inside the fit makes program
scores orthogonal to age by construction, rendering the association test
vacuous. Associations are tested post hoc instead.

```{r fit, eval = FALSE}
# scripts/fit_pilot.R wraps this per cell type with tryCatch isolation
x <- as_cell_program_data(pseudobulk, sample_metadata = meta)
fit <- fit_celltype_programs(
  x, loading_prior = "point_laplace", max_factors = 10,
  features = "variable", n_variable_genes = 2000,
  feature_scale = "logcounts", var_type = 1, seed = 20261016
)
fit <- canonicalize_programs(fit)
```

This yields 430–573 programs per cohort (after degenerate-factor handling;
e.g. KCL's Myeloid cDCs retains no programs). Age, sex, and CMV associations
are then tested per program with ordinary linear models on the program
scores (`scripts/assoc_programs.R`; BH-FDR within cell type; CMV dropped
where constant):

```{r assoc, eval = FALSE}
# per cell type and program, on the canonicalized scores:
fit_lm <- lm(score ~ age + sex + CMV, dd)   # dd: donors x (score, age, sex, CMV)
age_beta_per_10y <- coef(summary(fit_lm))["age", 1] / sd(dd$score) * 10
```

Age structure is widespread and scales with power: **44–56% of programs are
age-associated (FDR < 0.05)** in the 400–1000 donor cohorts (CIMA 55.8%,
OneK1K 43.6%, AIDA 43.5%) versus 3–19% in cohorts under 200 donors.

```{r fig-prevalence, eval = FALSE, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4}
# figures/fig_aging_age_prevalence.png
```

![Fraction of programs age-associated per cohort](figures/fig_aging_age_prevalence.png)

## The thymic-involution axis replicates across cohorts

Taking each cell type's strongest-age program and asking whether it
replicates in direction across the cohorts where it is significant: the
recent-thymic-emigrant programs decline essentially everywhere.

```{r rte, eval = FALSE}
# scripts/age_summary.R; per-cell-type table of strongest-age programs
```

| Cell type | Cohorts significant | Sign (neg/pos) | Median beta (SD/10y) |
|---|---|---|---|
| CD8+ RTE | 7 | **7 / 0** | −0.29 |
| CD4+ RTE | 7 | 6 / 1 | −0.32 |
| gd T naive | 7 | 6 / 1 | −0.32 |
| gd T Vd2 GZMK+ | 7 | **7 / 0** | −0.28 |
| CD8+ Temra | 7 | 5 / 2 | −0.22 |
| CD8+ Tem GZMK+ | 7 | 3 / 4 | +0.19 |

The CD8+ RTE program's loadings are canonical recent-emigrant biology
(SELL, CD8B, TRBC2, CD8A, CD7); the CD4+ RTE program adds SOX4 and LEF1.
This is the paper's central mechanism — thymic involution as the driver of
immune aging — recovered de novo by the EBMF pipeline.

```{r fig-rte, eval = FALSE, fig.width = 7.5, fig.height = 4.2}
# figures/fig_aging_rte_consistency.png
```

![Cross-cohort age betas of strongest-age programs](figures/fig_aging_rte_consistency.png)

Two interpretation notes. First, naive-compartment programs *increase* with
age (+0.32 SD/10y) — but their loadings are naive-vs-cytotoxic contrasts
(SELL/CCR7/LEF1 vs S100A4/NKG7/JUN), i.e. a shift in the naive pool's
internal makeup, complementary to the proportion-level naive decline the
paper reports. Second, the GZMK/GZMB health axis is a cell-type *proportion*;
at program level the Tem GZMK+ age signal marks its less-differentiated,
CD27+/LTB+ pole.

## Cross-cohort transfer: projection vs refit matching

The discovery fit (ABF300) is frozen (MR-0) and projected into each query
cohort (MR-1): each discovery program's score in the query is a fixed linear
combination of the query's pseudobulk profiles, with the discovery
preprocessing replayed. Matching projected programs to the query's own refit
programs by optimal assignment on |cor| gives the score-level transfer rate:

```{r project, eval = FALSE}
proj <- project_programs_to_cells(disc_fit, expr, cell_types,
                                  donors = donors, sample_metadata = meta,
                                  min_coverage = 0.9)
```

```{r fig-concordance, eval = FALSE, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 5}
# figures/fig_aging_concordance.png
```

![Matched program score concordance per query cohort](figures/fig_aging_concordance.png)

Median matched |cor| is 0.49–0.63 across all six pairs — moderate transfer,
with 30–39% sign flips (program orientation is arbitrary across fits).

## Why matched association profiles do not replicate — and what does

A natural test — correlate age betas across *matched* program pairs — fails
in every cohort (Spearman −0.07 to 0.17), **including at 981 donors where
beta noise is negligible**. The cause is structural, not statistical:
unsupervised EBMF decompositions distribute age-associated variance across
their K programs differently in each cohort (rotational freedom, adaptive
shrinkage, greedy factor addition). Program *identity* is cohort-specific
even when program *content* is conserved.

The projection sidesteps this: the discovery program's identity is pinned by
the frozen loadings, so testing `projected_score ~ age` in each query asks a
well-posed question — does *this fixed gene program* vary with age in the
query? Replication of discovery age hits (FDR < 0.05 in ABF300) on projected
scores:

```{r replication, eval = FALSE}
# scripts/projected_age_replication.R
```

| Query cohort | Discovery hits replicated (p<0.05, same sign) |
|---|---|
| CIMA (421) | **68%** |
| OneK1K (981) | 52% |
| UCSF (99) | 41% |
| AIDA (625) | 40% |
| SPAC (33) | 36% |

Null expectation is ~4%. Replication is real but partial — a core of
biologically coherent programs (RTE, gd T naive, gd T Vd2 GZMK+) replicates
near-universally, while the bulk regresses toward the null under winner's-curse
shrinkage and projection noise.

```{r fig-replication, eval = FALSE, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4}
# figures/fig_aging_replication.png
```

![Projected-score replication of discovery age hits](figures/fig_aging_replication.png)

## Gene lists are the wrong conservation unit

Finally, top-20 gene Jaccard for matched program pairs is low (median
0.03–0.13; ≥ 0.2 in only 8–36% of pairs): EBMF's dense, shrunk loadings make
top-N gene identity unstable even when the score subspace is conserved.
Conservation should be assessed at the score/subspace level, not by gene-set
overlap.

```{r fig-jaccard, eval = FALSE, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4}
# figures/fig_aging_jaccard.png
```

![Top-20 gene Jaccard of matched programs](figures/fig_aging_jaccard.png)

## The composition-level aging axis

Program scores capture within-compartment transcriptional shifts; cell
**proportions** capture a second, independent aging axis. Re-running the
per-donor models at the composition level (`prop ~ age + sex`, per cell
type; scripts in `analyses/immune_aging/scripts/`) shows the
thymic-involution signature even more universally than the program level:
CD8+ RTE proportions decline with age in **8/8 cohorts** (relative change
−22% to −70% per decade), CD4+ RTE in 8/8, CD8+ T naive in 8/8, and
γδ T Vd2 GZMK+ in 7/8 — mirroring the projected RTE program declines
above.

```{r fig-composition, eval = FALSE, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 6}
# figures/fig_aging_composition.png
```

![Relative change in cell-type proportion per decade of age](figures/fig_aging_composition.png)

The paper's **GZMK+/GZMB+ Tem ratio** behaves differently: its age
trajectory is cohort-inconsistent (log-ratio slope per decade −0.101 in
OneK1K, −0.078 in CIMA, −0.161 in SPAC, but **+0.157 in AIDA** — opposite
sign — and null in ABF300, KCL, UCSF, SoundLife). This is consistent with
the ratio acting as a **health-trajectory stratifier** rather than a
monotonic age effect. The **CMV effect** on the ratio, by contrast,
replicates cleanly where CMV status is recorded: in SoundLife, CMV+
serostatus shifts the log ratio by **−1.07 (p = 2.5e-11)** — CMV+ donors
carry a ~66% lower GZMK+/GZMB+ ratio — exactly the paper's claim. (KCL's
smaller, null estimate is diluted by its No_info stratum, kept as its own
level.)

```{r fig-tem-ratio, eval = FALSE, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4}
# figures/fig_aging_tem_ratio.png
```

![GZMK+/GZMB+ Tem ratio: age trajectory in OneK1K and CMV effect in SoundLife](figures/fig_aging_tem_ratio.png)

## Practical guidance

- **Freeze-then-project (MR-0/MR-1) is the right design for cross-cohort
  program claims**: it fixes program identity and makes replication tests
  well-posed.
- **Matched-refit association profiles are not a valid conservation metric**
  for unsupervised decompositions; use projected scores instead.
- **Report program-level and composition-level age structure separately** —
  they capture different biology (within-compartment shifts vs proportions).
- Small cohorts (n < 100) attenuate association replication severely; the
  per-cohort power table above is the honest caveat to carry.

## Reproducing

All scripts, committed result tables, and the exact commands (including the
portal data-access recipe and the registered operating point) live in
[`analyses/immune_aging/`](../../analyses/immune_aging/README.md). The batch
benchmark motivating the no-residualization design is in
`benchmarks/batch_adjustment/` (both the main and small-batch amendments
preregistered; neither rule fired; OLS default retained).
